The Preferences gear is gone from the Print history screen, after checking that every platform still has another way into JusPrin's Preferences window. It's committed as `df4ed7fc01` on `claude/gcode-print-history`, not pushed, with no PR.

## Step 1: is it safe? Yes, on all three platforms

**Windows** (I confirmed this in the running app, with Print history on screen):
- The title bar stays visible above the screen, with File, the menu icon, save, undo and redo.
- The Preferences item isn't under File; it's in the menu-icon dropdown. Choosing it opened JusPrin's Preferences window, not OrcaSlicer's.
- Ctrl+, pressed in the page also opened JusPrin's window.
- The harness now checks all of this on every `--print-history` run, and both checks pass.
- While testing I found a mistake in my own test, not the app: OrcaSlicer attaches that menu item's action to the menu itself, so I first sent the click to the wrong place and nothing opened. Sent the way a real click goes, it opens JusPrin's window.

**Linux** (checked by reading the code; I can't run it here): it uses the same title bar and the same menu item as Windows, which goes through the same JusPrin handler. Ctrl+, works through the page's own key handler, and through the window's key handler when focus is outside the page.

**macOS** (checked by reading the code): the app menu's "Preferences… ⌘," calls the same handler, so it opens JusPrin's window. Cmd+, is caught by the app menu, by the page's handler (which accepts Cmd as well as Ctrl), and by OrcaSlicer's own window key handler.

**One detail:** on Windows and Linux, OrcaSlicer's menu item shows Ctrl+P as its shortcut. Ctrl+P only works when the click focus is outside the page (on the 3D view or a native panel). Ctrl+, works either way.

## Step 2: the code

- **Change:** the gear button and `onPreferences` are removed. The bar keeps the back arrow and the title. The page's Ctrl+, handler is unchanged.
- **New test:** it checks that the history screen has no Preferences button and that Ctrl+, still asks for Preferences. I ran it before removing the gear and it failed, as it should.
- **Home page checks:** the type-check is clean, 110 of 110 tests pass, and `npm run build` succeeded.
- **Harness:** `--print-history C:\b\gph-review\history` passes with 0 failures, including the two new Preferences checks. I've sent you the new screenshots.

## Step 3: the design boards

I removed the gear from the top bar of history-01, history-02 and history-03 on the JusPrin v2 canvas, and changed nothing else. I re-read the canvas and the three files before editing, and they were unchanged since my earlier read. Only those three files were published (version 47), without `canvas.json`, and the comment watch is stopped.

## Step 4: Home's gear

As far as reaching Preferences goes, the same reasoning holds. The title bar menu and the page's Ctrl+, handler work the same on Home, because they belong to the whole window and the whole page, not to one screen. I only tested them with Print history showing, though, not on Home's gallery.

Discoverability matters more on Home:
- **Home is where people start.** Print history is a screen you visit from somewhere else; Home is the root screen of the app.
- **New users set up their agent in Preferences.** Preferences › Agent is where the agent is set up, and a new user looking at Home may not know to try Ctrl+, or an unlabeled menu icon.
- **The gear teaches the shortcut.** Its tooltip says "Preferences (Ctrl+,)".

If you remove Home's gear too, check that first run still leads people to agent setup some other way.

5:JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.
11:- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.
23:**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?
79:**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.
99:**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.
105:**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
109:**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.
111:**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.
113:**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?
121:1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.
133:An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

input.content:
Print history: record every G-code that leaves a project, show it, print it again

One record per G-code that left a project replaces the Sent events and
physical prints, which nothing outside tests ever wrote. It is shown on one
Print history screen, and any recorded G-code can be printed again from the
file the project kept. Nothing records, badges or draws a failure: a
printer reports a person's stop and a failed print the same way, so a print
that ended early simply never finishes. Slicing writes nothing.

The record (Agent/ManufacturingHistory, Agent/ProjectStateDocument)
- Keyed by the SHA-256 of the plate's sliced G-code, so the same slice
  exported and sent is one record. It holds where the G-code went (exports
  with the exported file's own hash; sends with the printer's name, whether
  the send started the print, when the transport confirmed it, and for a
  Bambu send the hash of the package it uploaded) and the prints the
  printer reported: started, finished. It also holds the slice's estimates
  and layer count, the presets, and the chat item it followed.
- A copy of each G-code that leaves is kept at <project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode,
  the newest 20 per project. A Bambu print also keeps the .gcode.3mf it
  uploaded, byte for byte (and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also
  sent), pruned with its G-code.
- A document holding the old "sent" and "physicalPrints" arrays loads and
  drops them (no shipped build wrote them).

Writers (Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder)
- Exports (OrcaSlicer's own and the export_file tool's) through the new
  EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED; Bambu prints and uploads through the jobs' finished
  events while their dialog is showing; print-host uploads through the
  queue's new enqueue observer and the queue dialog's progress at 100.
- Bambu printers are polled every two seconds whatever is on screen;
  Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker decides which report belongs to which send, and
  a finish of a project that is not open is written into its saved
  document. Print hosts record sends only.

Print history (HomeUI, Home/PrintHistory, Home/OrcaHomeBackend)
- A second screen of the Home page: one entry per G-code, grouped by day,
  with a row per destination (an export: matches, changed outside JusPrin,
  not found; a send: delivery and whether it started) and per print
  (Printing with its progress, Finished; a stopped one shows only when it
  started). Project and printer are removable filter chips over one list,
  with a search box. Its bar is Back and the title: Preferences is reached
  from the title bar's menu and Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).
- Ways in: a link in the gallery header, a line on each project card and
  printer card, one row on the project pane's Project tab (replacing its
  old Print history view), and a "history" link on each chat marker. Back
  returns to where it was opened from.
- Open in chat opens the project and scrolls its chat to the marker
  (reveal_item). Export... writes the kept copy and records it; Export again
  on a changed file writes a new file beside it, never over it.
- The chat shows one marker line where a G-code left, in place of the
  retired print card. The model reads the last ten records as printHistory.

Print again, and print_dialog_open
- Sends the kept file, never a fresh slice, always through OrcaSlicer's own
  send dialog; the person presses Send there and nothing in it is set.
- Bambu: the kept package goes to Select Machine the way the printer's file
  browser opens a file (Plater::update_print_required_data,
  EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW), with the dialog's new-print flag set so the
  job uploads the local file as a new print. Printing from the printer's
  storage is not used: the file name there is reused for every send of a
  project, so it cannot say which version would print.
- Print hosts with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog get a temporary copy
  of the kept G-code (the queue deletes what it uploads). ElegooLink,
  Creality Print, Flashforge's local API and use_3mf hosts are not offered
  Print again; PrusaConnect's readiness question is not asked.
- Offered only when the kept file is there and still hashes as kept;
  otherwise the entry says why and to slice again (a kept file changed on
  disk is logged as an error and never sent).
- print_dialog_open (in-app and MCP) opens the dialog for a plate's slice,
  refused with needs_step naming slice_start when it has none, or with
  gcode for a recorded G-code.

OrcaSlicer-owned files (all additive; no upstream line deleted, moved or
rewritten). The fork owns these seams; the policy is in fork files.
- Plater.hpp/.cpp: EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED, declared and defined, sent
  synchronously where an export of G-code (on_process_completed, when the
  run had an export path) or a sliced 3MF (export_gcode_3mf) reports it
  finished. on_process_completed keeps whether an export was scheduled in a
  local before reset_export() clears it.
- Utils/PrintHost.hpp/.cpp: PrintHostJobQueue::set_enqueue_observer, called
  with each job and its id as it is queued.
- SelectMachine.hpp/.cpp (17 lines): m_required_data_new_print_config
  beside m_required_data_file_path and its setter above set_print_type;
  after the combobox check the printer list stays enabled while it is set;
  in on_send_print after the storage branch it makes the job from_normal
  with job_data taken from the file (is_from_plater false, file and config
  paths, its plate index) and plate_data valid with the file plate's bed
  type. Nothing changes in PrintJob, SyncAmsInfoDialog or PrintFromType.

Rebase simulation: git merge-tree --merge-base=3ffb9585d2 upstream/main
against this commit and against its parent; see the PR or session notes
for the endpoint commits and result. Earlier runs: the Plater.cpp seam's
first form changed the export_3mf call line upstream has since rewritten
and was made additive; the SelectMachine setter first sat beside Show(bool),
which upstream has since made an override, and was moved above
set_print_type. In both cases the conflicting files then matched the parent's.

harness pictures and the gear removal), replayed onto jusprin-newui. One
merge resolution: the AgentUI rule .history-action, reworked on
jusprin-newui, belonged to the retired print card and has no users; it
stays removed, and its line in styles.test.ts with it.

Tests: test_project_state, test_print_outcome_tracker, test_print_history,
test_tool_coordinator (print_dialog_open), test_provider_agent,
test_project_status, test_project_pane_model, test_brand_tokens
(component.printHistory.listWidth), HomeUI and AgentUI page tests (the
no-failure-state and no-Preferences-button guards were seen to fail first),
and shell_integration_harness --print-history [capture-dir]: export, two
sends through Select Machine to the fake Bambu printer (which now records
the hash of the file it is sent), finish and fail through its control file,
the screen from the pane and from Home, Preferences from the title bar's
menu and Ctrl+, opening JusPrin's window, Export... and Export again, Open
in chat, and Print again uploading the kept package with the same bytes.
Not tested: a live Bambu printer, cloud sends, macOS and Linux.
